reviews.comment: This class were pretty tough within the summer 1 timeframe, grading criteria a little burry at points but email is your friend. Video critiques on your speeches are helpful for things to improve. He is so helpful and friendly o show dedication to the course and you will do good. He is one of my favorite professors I have taken at TAMU. Take him!
genuinely the goat, exams are pretty difficult but he lets you work in groups and use the textbook. hes a very chill prof and creates a really fun classroom dynamic. TAKE HIM!!!!

Professor Champine is amazing! Super sweet and makes classes fun and engaging. Classes are an attendance grade. Gives lots of extra credit and feedback. Reading assignments aren't too difficult.Two exams and one group project, and the exams are open note/open book. I'm taking him again for comm 305, I recommend if you have the chance to take him!

I had him for COMM 324. He is genuinley cares for his students! Be aware that there is A LOT of Perusalls, but other than that, I have no complaints about the class. There is one exam, and it is open notes, online, and we can do it with classmates. For the group project at the end of the semester, we could choose our groupmates. Super sweet prof.
Very chill guy. I took 324, attendance not mandatory, just a bunch of random assignments and one exam.

Changed coursework from his older classes and it has gotten unnecessarily hard. Heavy reading and lots of group work. He wasn't very clear with feedback and had lots of assignments. Quizzes were difficult even being open-note.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tyler Champine is definitely an above average professor. He is super down to earth and really funny and personable if you actually talk to him. His 210 class is a little disorganized and takes a little adaptation because its so unorthodox. Everyday is an open discussion forum and his homework is a lot of reading and projects. Just Participate!

I would take this class 100x if I could. Honestly, take this class even if you don't have to. Tyler was the coolest prof I have ever had, and the class was so worth it. There are 2 tests, but he lets you decide how you take them. 1 big group project and weekly reading on Perusall. The easiest course if you are just somewhat there. Take this class!!

I feel as if I wasted 1,000 + dollars taking this class. I did not learn a thing maybe because I never applied myself but I don't even think he enjoys his job. Seems like he shows up cause he has too. I would recommend if you aren't paying school but if you are it feels like a waste of money.

This professor has very unstable grading criteria, he also seems to grade extremely tough in a way that receiving an A is near impossible unless you spend an unnecessary amount of time on this class. The class is also organized in a way that makes half of the assignments that are due not show up in the assignments section.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you do a part of your assignment wrong, say goodbye to your points! He is an extremely tough grader and the course is assigned in a way that makes it near impossible to see what you need to do.

This class was a huge mess. Nice guy but kept changing how things were graded mid-semester & occasionally was difficult for no reason. It was a headache despite not being that difficult. If taught differently I prob would have liked it a lot because the material is interesting. He can be condescending sometimes and tries to play it off like humor.

Lectures and readings are really dense and philosophical with no foundation, in-class group assignments are busywork and confusing, and they're set up where you only "have" to do one reading but really need to read 4-5 to pass, insanely hard quizzes that changed format every time with no warning, and mass-accused us of cheating over spring break :(
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not the worst prof, but definitely not the best. Participation matters heavily, expect collaborated in-class assignments due within class time. Unclear grading criteria, beware of expectations that aren't included. The quizzes were the worst part. Format changed weekly, in addition to a cheating scandal during sb, this class is a total joke.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When asking him direct questions, he gives very confusing and unanswered answers. A LOT of group work. Each group reads a specific chapter in the textbook, but he expects you to know all the readings, which is impossible to read within a week. The quizzes are really hard, sometimes they don't say which questions you got wrong.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He LOVES group work. Thats what the entire course was based on. Most days we would just walk in and get to work with our groups. He is not helpful with feedback, his voice is SO boring and monotoned, and he takes forever on grading

Tyler is a great guy, but not a very organized professor. The syllabus doesn't dive deep into what he wants in your speeches, so it could be tough getting an A. But because of his tough grading, I do feel like a better public speaker.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally just show up and you'll get an A

He's a fun guy and I enjoyed being in his class, but his grading criteria was constantly fluctuating and he wasn't eager to offer feedback on assignments. I also had a bad group and that's difficult to work with.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Champine is nice outside of class but the course is unorganized and he is unhelpful. When asking him direct questions about content he dodges them and makes students even more confused. Quizzes are exceddingly difficult, no matter how much reading or prep you do before hand. Useless group work to try and learn content that would take weeks to read.

This class meets twice a week and is structured where one day is a lecture/quiz, and the other is in-class group work. Choose a good group of people who are willing to share their opinions in class. If you do your work and make friends with your group members you will do fine. I will say, he is very monotone and lectures are quite dull.

Great guy but the quizzes he gives you are about readings that weren't even assigned to you so you're just guessing. Attendance is mandatory; he only gives two excused absences; if you miss attendance points, it'll bring your grade down a lot. The lectures are very long and don't really have anything to do with the assignments he takes as grades.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has so much busywork. 30+ page readings with reflections due each class that are dense and hard to understand and have no application and are graded harshly. The actual assignments aren't bad but they're entirely unrelated to the readings and lectures. Such a waste of time. Champine is a nice guy but this class is terrible.

This guy is so annoying, he babbles on saying nothing, you dont learn anything, he's pretty bad at dealing with the class and has long response times on email. his sense of drama during a cheating problem was so annoying to anybody not involved. the worst part is he thinks what he's saying is important

He's an absolute chiller. I've taken him for a couple classes now and though sometimes his lectures are just reading and a little boring he's funny and nice and the classes are easy! Some people may not like the lack of structure but I loved it.

Tyler was a good professor and I loved the way his class was set up. If you were not present in class it didn't mean your grade was over. Tests were a little difficult, but honestly it mattered if you had a good group or not if you want to get an A. Curved tests a bit, but his TA REFUSED to give anyone an A.
this professor literally makes me want to cry. The TA is a hard grader also so don't expect him to make you smile either.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love the way this class was set up. You'll have a quiz in class once a week and a group case study in class once a week. Exams are not difficult if you study the quizzes and class lecture material. I would highly recommend this class.

Honestly this class wasn't terrible, you just need a good group. Projects every Thursday and quizzes on Tuesdays. It's all online so if you have a good group they can fill you in if you need to miss. He's chill, but his grading doesn't always seem the most fair so be sure to ask him questions about the final project in order to get a good grade.

quiz on a chapter every tuesday and group project case study every thursday. exams are difficult but he made them open note after the 1st one went horrible for everyone. never take this as an 8am. his lectures were really boring. if you get a bad group then you're done for because you have to rely on them to do their work every single week
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He does not care. I asked him questions about assignments in class and he really doesn't care about the class he just shrugs his shoulders. You work in groups for the whole semester and have weekly assignments, he graded hard in the first half but then just gave hundreds in the end. You WILL need the textbook for this class.

TAKE HIM! Champine is very personable and 210 is a small group-based class. He was always asking for our feedback and wanted to hear our opinions. Tests were confusing sometimes but nothing you should be scared about. You have notecards for the tests and you work with your group every time. He's awesome highly recommend!!!!

Class is graded on weekly group assignments, 3 open note exams, and a big group project towards the end of the semester. Attendance is only mandatory on Wednesdays for the weekly group assignment. Exams are application and can be pretty difficult. Tyler is very understanding, accommodating, and helpful! I would definitely take him again!

He made it sound like this class would be an easy A. As the semester went on people did bad on the tests which prompted him to make them open book and open note - and even so the average was a 60, indicating professor error. There are also weekly group case studies which he grades pickily and then leaves no comments. Cool guy, bad prof.

Really enjoyed his class! Group assignments once a week are doable and easy. Gives great feedback and listens well to his students. Exams and quizzes aren't horrible and material is found in the lectures and in the book. Would 10/10 take again!

Attendance isn't really mandatory, but you're working with a group so if you have to miss just communicate that with your group. Exams have been easy, go to class and take notes so you know what is on the tests. We made the test questions for the first exam he just changed the wording. Take him he is the best!!!

Champine was a really chill professor in class and although attendance was "mandatory" he never checked. In one class he gave extra credit to those who showed up. The only thing I did not like about the class was the contrast between the chill class and the harsh grading. He would give random Bs with little guidance on what looks like an A.

Attendance is mandatory, but we never did anything in class. There was only like 6 grades and he graded every writing assignment hard. Got an 89 in the class because I got a C on the final debate despite winning it unanimously.

Overall there was no work but his grading makes what should be an easy A very annoying. Would not recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super cool prof and very understanding. I hardly went to class and got a B but if you got regularly youll easily get an A. no final exam, just a project. exams are with a group and so are most of the assignments. most criteria is str8 from the textbook & theres a free online version. biggest tip is to just show up to class! hes great!

I like Professor Champine a lot as a person, he is such a cool guy and you'll have fun talking with him but the class was iffy. Instructions are very unclear on stuff but everything is doable if you put in the effort. Tests are taken with your group, speaking of groups, pick good people to be in yours!! This whole class is group work.

He is an amazing professor! His tests are purely based on the textbook, so his lectures are honestly just for fun. Such a good guy, I would recommend taking him! Make sure you make a good group at the beginning of the semester because you will be with them all semester!

This class is super dependent on attendance, so you have to be there for every class. The tests come straight from the textbook, the lecture material is pretty irrelevant. He gave pretty specific rubrics for group projects so you knew exactly what to do. Overall good class, easy A if you put in some effort.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's very down-to-Earth and forgiving. His class was interesting and we actually accomplished something cool through the group project we did as part of the class. All-around great guy.

Harder class than expected. Focus wasn't clear from the name, but information is useful. Be prepared for dense readings that are somewhat explained in the following class. Reading journals every week. Grading is pretty fair as long as you're good at restating an author's thesis and supporting evidence. A good Social Science credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tyler is a laid back professor (which is helpful when needing extensions on due dates, but difficult when trying to understand his vague directions). Many of the readings and class discussions have a political slant that can be pretty distracting and one-sided. Overall, its often a boring class, but is definitely doable.

Tyler was great! I wasn't sure what to expect at first, but I ended up really enjoying this class. There's a lot of reading you'll have to do but he makes sure you understand it in class. There are also a few papers you'll have to write but there were no exams or quizzes so that was nice. He's extremely reasonable, I recommend taking him 110%!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class this past semester and at first it seemed really scary with all of the papers expected. Tyler is really easy to work with and willing to help the students in anyway he can. He always allowed extra time if we needed it and gave great feedback so that our future papers could be better. Take Tyler, he's super caring and nice. :)
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: His rubrics were always very vague and he graded the assignments unnecessarily hard. For our group fishbowl (a major portion of our grade), my group did the best and we got an 87 and everyone else got an 80. His tests were really difficult, I would read the book, go to class, and study and never got above an 85. Take someone else if you can!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I got a B because I did two extra credit assignments not knowing you could only do one because he never said so. I even asked him what each extra credit was worth and he told me they were both worth 1 point added to my final grade and then I was slapped in the face with a B when grades were due. He then blamed me for not asking which I did.
Very chill class. Requires outside work (i.e. meeting w a nonprofit), but very rewarding and basically all group work.
